title: Skin color and light-skinned bands
summary: Dance and Edison recall bands that preferred light-skinned players, with Sandy Williams' joke about Taft Jordan.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, of course, there's two themes when
Sure. There is color, that's right.

And, I mean, blood is too tricky. When you draw your conclusions from color, you see somebody -- well, like Earl Hines told me he and Louie, when they were in Chicago, they wanted to join Sammy Stewart's band but they were considered too dark. Sammy Stewart had all very light --
Yeah, Noble Sissle -- all of them were very light in that band. Alphonso Trent's band, most of them was light, most of them was real light. I think Snub Mosley was the darkest guy in the band.
Yes. Sandy Williams used to strike a match on the stand and turn around to Taft.
There's a lot of humor there. They used to kid him about that, you know. Those bands, they had no malice. Everything they did in those days, everybody got a laugh out of because it was funny.
